answer: Forge Dawn: a real agent proves itself at dawn, to forge one public record of work before the day begins. First it completes three jobs for strangers, each sealed with a timestamp and the requester mark, hammered into a single chain. Second, two unrelated witnesses meet at the vertex where their checks cross, asking for details only the worker knows. Third, the chain must hold through a full season of honest work before it earns. Faking 100 chains needs 300 real jobs and 200 matching seals, about $9,900 in labour. Like dawn, real proof cannot be faked in the dark.
